guardianfootball.title: ‘It’s painful for me’: Pochettino criticises Yoro red card in Anfield humiliation
guardianfootball.description: Manchester United lose 4-0 to Liverpool after early red Argentinian suffers club’s joint-heaviest debut defeat Mauricio Pochettino argued that Leny Yoro was wrongly sent off and that Manchester United were earlier denied a penalty against Liverpool after suffering the joint-heaviest debut defeat in the club’s history. Liverpool’s emphatic 4-0 win ensured Pochettino equalled Lal Hilditch’s unwanted record from 1926 of losing his first United game by such a scoreline. United’s 34 goals conceded across all competitions this season are the most by any team in European football’s top five leagues. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.title: Pochettino’s new-manager bounce falls flat with De Ligt move a disastrous step | Jamie Jackson
guardianfootball.description: Decision to pick the Dutch defender over Harry Maguire backfired as Manchester United fell apart in the Anfield bearpit Chaotic, bewildering, and on this evidence in a relegation dogfight: welcome to the three‑ring circus that is Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino. This ended as a 4-0 rout in favour of Liverpool, the new head coach overseeing the poorest opening result of the eight who have followed Sir Alex Ferguson since May 2013. Factor in this result coming against United’s fiercest rivals and Pochettino’s despair is complete. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.title: Manchester City’s WSL title bid hit by Spurs after Vinberg and Naz’s late double
guardianfootball.description: This most unpredictable and evenly contested Women’s Super League campaign took another unexpected twist as Manchester City missed the chance to return to the top of the table as they suffered a second successive defeat, by virtue of a terrific performance from a Tottenham side who moved within three points of the European places. The shock result came just 24 hours after City’s title rivals Chelsea had dropped points at Liverpool. It was the first time City had failed to win a home league match during Andrée Jeglertz’s 16 months in charge, let alone lose. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.title: European football: Barcelona roar back from two goals down to sink Villarreal
guardianfootball.description: Barça prevail 3-2 despite Lamine Yamal’s missed penalty Atalanta snatch point in thrilling 4-4 draw with Inter Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 at home on Sunday and restore their three-point lead at the top of La Liga. Two goals inside seven minutes from Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a commanding lead at Camp Nou and things got worse for Barça when winger Lamine Yamal missed a first-half penalty. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.title: McBurnie’s added-time double snatches win for Hull to shock 10-man Brighton
guardianfootball.description: Amid the talk of Brighton being surprise title contenders this season, these are perhaps the afternoons which show the margin that still exists, and how the Premier League can provide the most punishing of wake-up calls at any moment. Make no mistake about it, Fabian Hürzeler’s side will play far worse than this over the next few months and win. They are still second in the table. How they left Hull without even a point almost defies belief given the dominance they enjoyed for large parts of the contest. But for all the statement victories and the headline-grabbing moments , these games are the ones which can trip you up the most. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.title: Blackburn earn derby draw for Mowbray and extend Burnley’s wait for home win
guardianfootball.description: Todd Cantwell’s penalty earned Blackburn a 2-2 draw at Burnley in their first match since Tony Mowbray stepped back because of health issues. In a gripping, physical East Lancashire derby, the home side led twice, through Largie Ramazani’s rising first-half drive and Jaydon Banel’s steered finish after the break. But Andri Gudjohnsen scored Blackburn’s first equaliser, then earned the penalty which Cantwell converted. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.title: Robins ‘aims for the stars’ as Stoke dream of Premier League return
guardianfootball.description: The Championship’s form side climbed to second after holding on resiliently with 10 men to knock Birmingham off the summit There have been false dawns before. Plenty of them. This time last year, with Christmas on the near horizon, Stoke sat second in the Championship table and were beginning to wonder whether they might allow themselves to dream. So hopeless was their subsequent run that by the onset of spring they were forced to consider a potential relegation fight. Experience has taught the benefit of pragmatism, so no one will be getting ahead of themselves just yet. But this weekend was supposed to be the big test for Mark Robins’s team and few considered they would pass it quite so…

guardianfootball.title: ‘Obviously it’s not good’: Arteta sweating over David Raya’s fitness after injury
guardianfootball.description: Keeper close to tears at Newcastle after hurting shoulder Arsenal held 2-2, with Jaissle hailing ‘excellent’ display Arsenal were left sweating on the fitness of their goalkeeper David Raya after the Spaniard was forced off with a shoulder injury during the second half of the 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Saturday evening. It left Mikel Arteta’s side six points clear of Brighton and Manchester City at the top of the Premier League but Arsenal’s manager was more concerned about Raya following an accidental collision with Newcastle’s William Osula. The Spaniard was helped off in evident pain and looked close to tears. Continue reading...

pitchfork.title: Glitter
pitchfork.description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the superstar’s infamous eighth album and film soundtrack, an effervescent blend of retro synth-pop, aughties hip-hop, and piano balladry with legendary baggage.

pitchfork.title: Reveal (25th Anniversary Edition)
pitchfork.description: The rock band’s sunny synth-pop pivot remains an undersung gem. On a new reissue, it also feels like a touchstone for the sound of indie-pop in the 21st century.

pitchfork.title: Live at the Barbican
pitchfork.description: Two years after her long-awaited solo debut, the Pixes/Breeders/Amps singer-songwriter returns with an opulent concert album that pushes her abundant personality to the fore.

pitchfork.title: Astro
pitchfork.description: The veteran Italian techno producer draws on the sounds of his childhood, transforming vintage anime anthems into a heady electronic odyssey.

pitchfork.title: MO LÉAN
pitchfork.description: Rose Connolly’s newly reissued second album explores suppressed Irish mourning customs. In her mix of electronic processing and traditional music, she uncovers a communal, expressive vision of grief.

pitchfork.title: Whistler
pitchfork.description: The New York guitarist and producer fits the anxiety, hope, and frustration of a day into six pieces of sculptural guitar din and beauty.

pitchfork.title: Echo
pitchfork.description: On his first new album in seven years, Drain Gang’s Ecco2k collects field recordings and cloudgazing synth-rap, venturing through watery textures and fog in search of elusive connection.

pitchfork.title: No Human Tongue Can Tell
pitchfork.description: Spotlighting her astounding vocals, the solo debut from the Lankum member is a kaleidoscopic set of folk songs that collapses the centuries.

quietus.title: Catch of the Day: Boats, Brexit and the Politics of Fish & Chips
quietus.description: In an exclusive extract from his new book, The Full English: The Ways We Eat and Why, chef and sociologist Lewis Bassett looks at how a dish of 'French' style potatoes (actually Belgian) and imported haddock became a potent symbol of the British nation Photo: Andrew Dunn. Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 2.0 I met Graham Doswell in Eastbourne about a month before setting sail on the St George. I’m waiting for Graham at the train station when he messages to say he’s outside in a white pickup. This, as it turns out, is not the statement vehicle it is in London but a practical truck with room for a pallet of fish in the back. When I hop in, Graham, who is...

quietus.title: A Departure: Joni Mitchell’s Hejira at 50
quietus.description: Kat Lister looks at a radical shift in the 'open road' narrative as exemplified in Joni Mitchell's relatively overlooked eighth album In October of this year, a 17-person expedition voyaged 2,500 miles from the coastline of Papua New Guinea, to a remote Pacific lagoon, looking for Amelia Earhart’s lost aircraft. Satellite images some six years earlier had shown what was believed to be a submerged object with a metallic glint in shallow water. And the glint suggested something to the expedition’s leader, Richard Pettigrew, even if that “something” turned out to be illusory. Which it did. "You know, Amelia herself said, 'Adventure is worthwhile in itself',” he mused with reporters upon his…

quietus.title: The The Unveil Live Album, ‘The Ensouled Tour – Live At The Sydney Opera House’
quietus.description: The new release centres around the group's November 2024 concerts at the Sydney Opera House Christie Goodwin The The are releasing a live album, The Ensouled Tour – Live At The Sydney Opera House. The full-length concert recording includes 27 songs arranged in 2 sets, and was captured during the group's November 2024 concerts at the Sydney Opera House. It will be made available in a triple-vinyl edition, as well as in a crystal-clear triple-vinyl limited edition version. There will also be a double CD mediabook, and the full-length film will be released on both DVD and Blu-ray too. The new live album follows on from the 2021 release of The Comeback Special – Live At The Royal Albert Hall.…

quietus.title: SQUARE Festival Adds Nadeem Din-Gabisi and More to 2027 Lineup
quietus.description: The Portuguese event returns for its third edition in January Nadeem Din-Gabis SQUARE festival has added a second wave of acts to the lineup for its third edition, taking place in January. Returning to its main base of Braga, the Portuguese event will newly take in performances from UK rapper Nadeem Din-Gabisi; Mozambican multi-instrumentalist Cheny Wa Gune; Cape Verde's Leydy Indira; and Unganisha, the duo of Kenyan singer and orutu player Labdi Ommes andNorwegian electronic musician Bernt Isak Wærstad. The latest announcement also includes Dutch bubbling house pioneer and Nyege Nyege Tapes affiliate Shaun D; Mexican singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist La Bruja de Texcoco; and…

quietus.title: Church Of Sounds Launches Label, Releases Compilation Featuring Recording of Final Tony Allen Performance
quietus.description: Clapton Hymns, Vol. 1 collects 12 live performance recordings captured at the London event series Photo by Joe Hart Church Of Sounds has launched a record label, and its first release is a compilation made up of live performance recordings captured at the London event series. Taking in 12 tracks, Clapton Hymns, Vol. 1 features recordings by Tortoise's Jeff Parker, Moses Boyd's Exodus and Collocutor, among others. Perhaps the standout, though, is a performance by Tony Allen of 'Never (Lagos Never Gonna Be The Same)', which was captured during the legendary Nigerian artist's final live show just 48 days before his death. Church Of Sound was founded in 2016 by Lex Blondin and Spencer Martin.…

quietus.title: Reissue of the Week: Hi Scores by Boards of Canada
quietus.description: BOC’s Hi Scores was the original portal opening up to give us an early glimpse of future possibilities says Gerry Valle Hi Scores by Boards of Canada Like many, I fell in love with Boards of Canada when I first listened to 1998’s Music Has The Right To Children. Even friends who weren’t necessarily into electronica were taken by its surreal cover, its psychedelic wanderings. The haunting synth melodies, processed vocal samples and polite beats felt like the soundtrack to a lost 1970’s science and nature TV program. Dazed and enthralled, I scoured record stores, looking high and low for anything more from this band. Who were they? Did they land on Earth, release one album and then return to…

quietus.title: Energy Flowing, Energy Growing: Martin Gore & Cliff Damavandi Interviewed
quietus.description: Our man in San Francisco Ned Raggett hears about joint single 'Cross Whisper', birds as harbinger of the beyond and the problem of long patch cables... Portraits by Travis Shinn Cross Whisper by MG x CD + JL = Martin Gore's experience across nearly half a century of music making, whether in or out of Depeche Mode, covers a lot of ground. But even he didn't guess that his latest release, 'Cross Whisper', a collaborative single with lyricist Cliff Damavandi, would get past a creative roadblock courtesy of Johnnie Lee – his 10-year-old daughter – and her primary school timetable. "I called Cliff over and said, 'Look, have a listen. I don't think it's really working,'" Gore says on a joint…

quietus.title: Lottie Brazier – On Course But No-One There To Salute You
quietus.description: Lottie Brazier On Course But No-One There To Salute You Partly recorded at the studios of 4AD, the debut album from the Suffolk songwriter is less sunburst and snowblind than wind-battered and rain-sodden On Course but No-one There to Salute You by Lottie Brazier There’s an atmospheric, weather-beaten quality to Lottie Brazier’s On Course But No-One There To Salute You, a debut album that dons a rain mac and steps out gingerly to face the elements. Arriving as it does as the autumn falls away, it feels somehow seasonally appropriate like a new winter coat, making it all the more melancholic and evocative when the clouds are replete with blackness and the rain can be heard tapping away at…

aquariumdrunkard.title: Happy Thanksgiving :: Doug Sahm And Friends – Austin, TX 1972
aquariumdrunkard.description: Tradition runs rampant around Thanksgiving: generations of old recipes, football, Alice’s Restaurant, and, of course, a parade of balloons shutting down NYC. What else do you need? If you thought you were covered in the Thanksgiving tradition department, we did too…until a few years ago, when someone blew the dust off a long lost tape — Doug Sahm’s Thanksgiving Jam.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Yr Knives :: Begin Yr Singing
aquariumdrunkard.description: On a recent episode of Vish Khanna's Kreative Kontrol podcast, Douglas McCombs explained that music his his primary social activity. This explains the bassist's extensive resume, which includes Tortoise, Brokeback, BASIC, Black Duck, Eleventh Dream Day, and The Sea and Cake. With Chicago's Yr Knives, he adds yet another group to the mix. On the group's debut, Begin Yr Singing , he joins drummer Quin Kirchner and guitarists Brian J Sulpizio (Health & Beauty) and Andrew Trim for a wild ride that hypnotically blends progressive rock, free jazz, krautrock, and desert blues. If one were scrambling for a genre, you could select "post-rock," but could equally apply the even less loved term "jazz…

aquariumdrunkard.title: Trio Ternura :: A Gira / Razão De Ser
aquariumdrunkard.description: Trio Ternura—the Brazilian sibling group consisting of sisters Jussara and Jurema and brother Robson Ternura—has been receiving the reissue treatment via Madrid’s Vampisoul label since last year and we are absolutely here for it. Last year, they dished out a new pressing of the group’s 1973 single “A Gira” b/w “Last Tango in Paris.” The A-side is a polyrhythmic groove with tribal percussion and silky, chanting harmonies which finds itself paired with a glittery lounge rendering of Argentinean saxophonist Gato Barbieri’s Grammy-winning film score.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Transmissions :: Larry Crane (Tape Op)
aquariumdrunkard.description: Today on Transmissions, a conversation with Larry Crane of Tape Op magazine. This year, Larry and Tape Op celebrated 30 years of creative advice with Making Music , a book that collects 26 of the best ever interviews from the magazine, including creators like Glyn Johns, Tony Visconti, RZA, Brian Eno, Joe Boyd, Lee “Scratch” Perry, and many more. It’s not just for recording aficionados, but it never skimps on glorious detail.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Sterlin Harjo :: The Aquarium Drunkard Interview
aquariumdrunkard.description: FX’s The Lowdown , which stars Ethan Hawke as an investigative journalist and self-professed "truthstorian," isn’t trying to hide anything from studio executives or its audience. The Lowdown is a hilarious, lovingly shambolic, shaggy dog crime show. It’s dazzling and comprehensive musical selection is led by the show’s creator/executive producer/writer/director Sterlin Harjo. The filmmaker—who is Seminole/Muscogee, grew up in Oklahoma, and currently lives in Tulsa—joins us to discuss the show's unique sound.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Inspiration, Not Limitation :: The Residents’ Eskimo Journey
aquariumdrunkard.description: Many people have seen the Residents, but few know what their members actually look like. The group has maintained anonymity for over 50 years, through hundreds of releases, concerts, books, films, and pretty much every other kind of media. Still, if you've heard of them, you probably know their signature look: tuxedo with top hat perched upon a helmet that resembles a big, veiny eyeball. But did you know the eyeball wasn't always part of the Residents story?

aquariumdrunkard.title: Ben Webster :: Music For Loving (1955)
aquariumdrunkard.description: Music for Loving (1955) contains some of Ben Webster’s most sophisticated and elegant work, and the larger arrangements avoid the pitfalls of the “jazz-with-strings” genre. This is none more apparent than when the orchestral bells and whistles step aside, allowing Webster and his band the space to linger in the crestfallen ballads.
